prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop landing page UI concept for Izge, edge-to-edge landscape 1536x1024, crisp readable interface text, no browser frame, device or desk. Izge finds consequential connections across company records and brings evidence into daily collaboration. A company buyer should witness a discovery, inspect why it matters, and choose Try demo. Lead with an immersive working-day scene across the page, not a split hero or a centered slogan over cards. One dominant product event: an Izge finding interrupts a quiet workspace: '18 hours delivered. Never invoiced.' The finding displays '₺36,000 + VAT / Potential billing to review', with clearly readable 'Demo scenario · Subject to commercial approval'. Three compact inspectable source excerpts ground it: Contract '₺2,000/hour', Delivery '18 hours', Invoice 'Maintenance only'. Show controls 'Trace evidence' and 'Discuss with team', not a chatbot prompt as the hero. A restrained side conversation shows Ece asking Selin to review; a secondary private Izge conversation is visible as navigation, not competing content. Navigation: Izge wordmark, Product, How it works, EN / TR, Try demo. Short page hook: 'The colleague who notices what slips through.' Slate-black ground and pearl type, soft blue for selected evidence and a warm muted attention marker only on the new finding. Contemporary humanist sans and precise product surfaces; cinematic hierarchy without glow, glass clutter or decorative particles. The start of the next section reveals source detail and an accountable next action. No fabricated revenue recovery or customer claim.
Strict correction: this is ONLY a flat website screenshot. Absolutely no photographic people, offices, furniture, desks, rooms or scenery anywhere. The entire backdrop is flat slate-black website canvas. Show the short page hook above the finding and full navigation. Company name Atlas, September 2026; do not introduce other customers or claims about similar cases. The interface itself carries the experience.
notes: Concept only. Jira/NetSuite labels, extra finding counts and secondary source metadata are image-model inventions, not supported integrations or product claims; exclude from implementation.
approval: User selected original composition, with finding → evidence → team discussion as scroll progression; actual app truth overrides invented integrations, counts and source metadata.
